record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Matrix Theory Arising in Linear Systems and Control
record.context_brief: reduced-order LQG algebraic equations and stabilization
record.original_question: For the reduced-order linear-quadratic-Gaussian controller problem with controller state dimension n_c < n, analyze the coupled algebraic equations (6.31)-(6.34) and determine when there exist controller matrices A_c, B_c, and C_c such that the closed-loop block matrix [[A, B C_c], [B_c C, A_c]] is asymptotically stable. The source presents the equations and explicitly links their analysis to this unresolved existence problem.

evidence.quote: Again a seemingly minor extension of the standard theory has major consequences with respect to the algebraic matrix equations to which it gives rise.

As with the static output-feedback problem, it can also be expected that the analysis of (6.13)-(6.34) is related to the existence of gains A_c, B_c, C_c such that the closed-loop dynamics matrix [A  BC_c; B_c C  A_c] is asymptotically stable.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$, $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$, and $C \in \mathbb{R}^{\ell\times n}$ be given matrices defining the linear time-invariant plant $\dot{x}=Ax+Bu,\ y=Cx$. Fix an integer $n_c$ with $1 \le n_c < n$ (a strictly reduced controller order). For controller matrices $A_c \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c\times n_c}$, $B_c \in \mathbb{R}^{n_c\times \ell}$, $C_c \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n_c}$, form the closed-loop dynamics matrix
$$\tilde{A}(A_c,B_c,C_c) \;=\; \begin{bmatrix} A & B C_c \\ B_c C & A_c \end{bmatrix} \in \mathbb{R}^{(n+n_c)\times(n+n_c)}.$$
The matrix $\tilde{A}$ is called asymptotically stable if every eigenvalue has strictly negative real part.

Problem. Give verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions on the triple $(A,B,C)$ and the integer $n_c$ under which there exist matrices $A_c, B_c, C_c$ (of the prescribed dimensions) such that $\tilde{A}(A_c,B_c,C_c)$ is asymptotically stable. In particular, characterize the solvability of this reduced-order dynamic output-feedback stabilization problem and relate it to the existence of solutions of the coupled algebraic Riccati/Lyapunov equations that arise from the first-order optimality conditions for the reduced-order linear-quadratic-Gaussian (LQG) controller synthesis problem.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of existence/synthesis of a fixed (reduced) order stabilizing dynamic output-feedback compensator is known to be computationally intractable: the associated matrix-inequality feasibility problem has been shown to be NP-hard, and no tractable verifiable necessary and sufficient conditions are known. Research continues via LMI-based sufficient conditions and coupled Riccati-equation approaches, but a complete characterization remains open.

status_evidence.title: Computational complexity of a problem arising in fixed order output feedback design
status_evidence.snippet: The matrix inequality problem arising in fixed order output feedback control design has been shown to be NP-hard.
status_evidence.claim: The fixed-order output feedback design feasibility problem is NP-hard, indicating that no tractable general characterization is currently known.

status_evidence.title: Static Output Feedback Controller Design
status_evidence.snippet: Fixed order output feedback stabilization... remains one of the most important open questions in control engineering.
status_evidence.claim: Fixed/reduced-order output feedback stabilization is widely regarded as an open problem in control theory.
